To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
we present the first algorithm that jointly searches for DNN architecture and accelerator configuration, and achieves state of the art performance on Xilinx FPGAs.

we propose a novel hardware aware NAS algorithm, which can automatically search the DNN subgraph and accelerator configuration that minimizes the latency for a given set of hardware resource constraint, and our algorithm achieves state of the art performance on Xilinx FPGA.

1) We propose a novel hardware aware NAS algorithm, HAO, that incorporates integer programming into search algorithm for efficient DNN inference on FPGAs 2) We use integer programming to directly output the optimal accelerator configuration given the resource constraints and the accuracy latency trade off for DNN subgraphs 3) We show that our algorithm achieves state of the art hardware performance and accuracy for image classification on Xilinx ZU3EG FPGA
In summary, our research is concerned with
the problem of hardware-aware neural architecture optimization (HAO) and we make the following contributions:
the design of an algorithm for automatic hardware aware neural architecture optimization.
the problem of automatic hardware aware NAS.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
our work is a novel and effective algorithm to search for optimal DNNs for hardware implementation.
our work is a novel approach that combines integer programming and neural architecture search to optimize hardware and software performance for efficient DNN inference on FPGAs.
our work incorporates integer linear programming into the search algorithms to prune the design search space and generate the optimal accelerator configuration.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
our algorithm can automatically find the optimal neural architecture and hardware accelerator for a given DNN subgraph.
our work is a new approach to solve the problem of DNN hardware co design.
we propose a new hardware aware NAS algorithm that can search for optimal accelerator configurations for a given neural network architecture.
The main takeaway from our work is that
integer programming can be used for pruning the search space and finding the optimal accelerator configuration.
integer programming can be used to prune the design search space for DNNs and hardware accelerator implementation and can be used as an alternative approach to NAS.
integer programming can be used as a fast alternative to learning based approaches for efficient hardware accelerator search.
